# Kbd

A keyboard key or shortcut, shown as text.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill odv-pill-out">Left out of Accessible first</span> Kbd tells people the shortcut for an action. Here people do this once or twice a year, and nobody remembers the interface from last time. <span class="odv-instead">Use instead: <a href="./label">Label</a></span></p>

## When to use it

- **Use it when:** Telling people the shortcut for an action.
- **Not when:** Decoration, or the only way to discover an action.

Instead:

- [Command](./command.md): Where shortcuts are often listed.

## Words

- Use common words. Explain any term you must use.
- One idea per sentence. Put the action first.
- Never blame the person.
- Use: Continue, Change, Start, You. Avoid: Invalid, Utilise, Submit, Error code.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Continue
- `content.action.cancel`: Go back
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Start a new application

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add kbd
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Variables

Every token Kbd reads, from its code: the variable, the semantic token it aliases, and where that ends in the theme.

### Read straight from the system

Kbd has no variables of its own yet; it reads these system tokens directly.
